name: Aruba
summary: Spanish rule, Dutch rule and a succession of brief British interruptions.
notes: The 1986 status aparte made Aruba a constituent country within the Kingdom, not independent. Miranda’s visits in 1806 are recorded as expeditions rather than sovereign Venezuelan annexations.

events.title: Spain claims Aruba
events.detail: Ojeda’s expedition reached the Caquetío islands.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Spanish colonial administration
events.detail: The ABC islands entered Spanish colonial administration after forced Indigenous removals.
events.uncertainty: Regional administrative date; no single island-wide conquest is implied.

events.title: Dutch possession begins
events.detail: The Dutch West India Company took Aruba as a dependency of Curaçao.

events.title: A brief British occupation
events.detail: British forces held Aruba for about a week.

events.title: Dutch administration resumes
events.detail: British forces withdrew after an occupation of about a week.
events.uncertainty: The exact days are unresolved. Arrival and withdrawal are both recorded at month precision; their plotted positions coincide.

events.title: Miranda uses Aruba as a base
events.detail: The Venezuelan revolutionary’s expeditions briefly occupied the island; no lasting government followed.

events.title: A longer British occupation
events.detail: The Napoleonic Wars brought another seizure.

events.title: Aruba returned to the Dutch
events.detail: The postwar settlement was implemented on the island.

events.title: Status aparte
events.detail: Aruba left the Netherlands Antilles to become a country within the Kingdom.
